description: cross-cylinders-common's two cylinders with the turn 1.26e-5° past −90°: the turned seam meets the first wall 2.2e-7 either side of a point 2.2e-7 from the crossing vertex (0, R, 0), so its two crossings lie 3.1e-7 from that vertex and 4.4e-7 from each other — just past the two tolerances within which the seam's touch joins the crossing vertex and the three are one (seam-a-tolerance-from-crossing-fuse). The solid is the Steinmetz solid of cross-cylinders-common, as at every turn. Arris fails: the checker's L4, a loop of zero signed area — the piece of the turned wall between the seam and the two ellipses, a triangle a few tolerances across whose vertices are three and apart, is a face of the result whose (u, v) polygon does not resolve it. It fails from two tolerances to about 2.6, not at every turn in between, and the fuse at the same turns does not (found in plans/c3-tolerance-apart step 2b). The desired result is the body at a generic turn, the sliver face kept, left out or refused by name — the sliver decision of docs/BACKLOG.md. The tolerances are stated at 2e-7 because Open CASCADE leaves the sliver out: its volume is 4.7e-7 (8.9e-8 relative) under 16R³/3, its area 1.4e-6 (8.7e-8) under 16R², within the lint's cross-check of the closed forms, but further from a body kept whole than 1e-9

analytic.counts_differ: Open CASCADE reports 5/8/5, a vertex, two edges and a face fewer than a generic turn's 6/10/6, which Arris keeps: it leaves the sliver between the seam and the two ellipses out
